description:
Journey — create, then bind a model to every creature slot (get carries the creatures report) and set the controls: action=controls applies the control scheme of the gameplay, a proposal to adapt. Before telling the user the game is done: gripforge_game_audit. Manage Game Kit projects (gkp_…): the container holding installed kits, their lockfile, asset bindings and data collections. action=list lists the workspace projects; create needs name and takes a preset (see gripforge_gamekit_search; adventure is the reference game of game.engine) or an explicit kits map — every new project gets game.engine first (the engine of the game: scenes, archetypes, scripts, life cycle; its answer carries the engine start pack { structure, scene, blocks, order, next, rules } and added, the kits installed for dependencies), then the default kits ui.menu (title / pause / options / load and save screen), input.remap (key remapping), settings.graphics (graphics options), ui.prompts (on-screen key prompts that follow remapping and the gamepad), ui.endscreen (end screen and credits), save.persistence (save slots, quick save, autosave), audio.core (game audio: mixer, music, effects, event → sound table), i18n.text (game texts in the player’s language: translation tables in the translations collection, ICU plurals) ui.theme (the design of every interface as kit config: colours, font, shapes, key glyphs; unset = built-in look) and input.virtualpad (the on-screen gamepad of touch screens, mode auto: shown on a touch screen without a gamepad, Touch controls tab) and display.fullscreen (the game in fullscreen: F11, the Options entry, start in fullscreen with atStart, the player’s choice saved), asset.preload (the files of the game loaded in phases — first playable frame, background, next scene ahead — each file once, checked; progress as state and events shown by ui.menu, ui.endscreen and hud.action) and asset.cache (the files kept on the device between visits: IndexedDB, then Cache Storage with a service worker, then the HTTP cache; quota and eviction) and, on web, ai.navigation (the paths of the game over its real collision geometry: route and steer for NPCs, enemies and click-to-move), addedBy default: keep and configure them (never recode a pathfinding: ask ai.navigation and adapt its config, the hook navigation.plan and the event navigation.blocked; never recode an asset loader, a download queue or a cache: adapt their rules, asset_preload documents, scenes ahead and cache quota instead), leave one out ({ "ui.menu": false }) or remove it only if the user asks. They hold for EVERY game, a compiled module with its own page or a custom page included: that page mounts the menu, Options › Controls and Video, fullscreen and the prompts from the bindings through the kits’ web views (gripforge-ui.mjs, GET /api/v1/hud) or their adapter, never its own copy; get returns the full ProjectDetail (installed kits, bindings, capabilities, missing, playUrl); bind maps asset slots to Library items (lib_…, null to clear); data reads a collection or upserts / removes documents validated against the kits’ schemas (replace=true swaps the whole collection); controls reads or sets the controls: without scheme it returns the control schemes of the catalogue (fps, third_person, moba_click, top_down, platformer, fighting, vehicle, rts, point_click: movement by keys or by click, what the mouse is for, expected actions and keys, touch layout), the project scheme, the one its kits suggest, every action with its effective key and the keys two actions share in one mode (warnings with a proposed reassignment, never a refusal — also in get → report.controls); with scheme and dry_run=true it returns the diff of keys the scheme would write; with scheme alone it applies it (input.actions overrides marked source: scheme, the touch layout of input.virtualpad, the help bar of ui.prompts). Choose the scheme from the kind of game, never from a kit default: 
Kits offer capabilities that can be switched off and tuned; the game makes one high-level gameplay choice and enables only the coherent set that choice needs: what is not chosen is off and invisible, and no kit default is imposed on the game. The generic modules propose choices, the request picks one: name the kind of game, take its control scheme from the table below (usually the only one allowed), and embed only what that scheme uses on each device — its input sources, its on-screen controls on a touch screen, its settings (remapping, sensitivity, inversion, capture, dead zone only where the scheme uses them). Every option is a choice of the request too: the network input frame is embedded only for a multiplayer game, each other option only when asked. Write the choice into the project: gripforge_game_project create with controls=<scheme>, or action=controls scheme=<scheme> on an existing game (dry_run first, reset=true to drop old key overrides). A dungeon crawler is played with the mouse, not on W A S D. In play, input.scheme (a default kit) implements that choice: it follows the device in hand (keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch) with the variant of the scheme for it, takes the vehicle scheme while the player drives, gives the input to the interface while a menu, a dialogue or a text field is open, and the Options show per device only the controls the scheme uses; tune it within the choice (input.scheme allowed: the closed list the player may switch between, usually one; variants; composites for held / double / charged / chorded / combo actions), never by enabling every option.
Gameplay choices (kind → control scheme, per device):
- MOBA → `moba_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: tap_world, settings: touch_layout). A hero is ordered with the mouse (right click to move / attack, abilities toward the cursor); a gamepad moves it with the stick. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style bold, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Real-time strategy → `rts` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: click to move, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: tap to move, on screen: stick + buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Units are selected and ordered with the cursor; nothing is moved with W A S D. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, moveMarker, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Dungeon crawler / action RPG seen from above → `arpg_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Played with the mouse: click to walk, click an enemy to attack, right click for the special; the left stick on a gamepad, a tap on a touch screen. W A S D is not the default for this genre. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, cursor, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Top-down shooter / twin-stick roguelike → `top_down` (mouse+keys: WASD, right click = aim, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Constant dodging needs direct movement (W A S D / left stick) with the cursor or right stick to aim. The game may also allow: arpg_click. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Point-and-click adventure → `point_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). A free cursor: click where to go and what to use. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, moveMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- First-person shooter / survival → `fps` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). W A S D and the captured mouse to look (right stick on a gamepad). Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: highlight, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Third-person action / open world → `third_person` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). W A S D relative to the camera and the captured mouse (right stick) to turn it. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Platformer → `platformer` (mouse+keys: WASD, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: virtual stick, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Direct movement and jump, no pointer. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail, sound.
- Fighting → `fighting` (mouse+keys: WASD, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: virtual stick, on screen: buttons, settings: touch_layout). One key per blow, no pointer. No interaction.feedback.
- Racing / vehicles → `vehicle` (mouse+keys: vehicle, settings: remap; gamepad: vehicle, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: vehicle, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Throttle, brake and steering; no pointer. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail.
Per device: the cursor per kind of target only with a mouse; on a gamepad the prompt shows the button of the active gamepad, on a touch screen the text alone (ui.prompts / input.actions promptFor); the designated target comes from input.scheme target() (cursor, aim axis, stick).
Interactions must be visible. Install interaction.feedback for any game with interactive objects (not for a pure fighting game) and set its elements from the gameplay table row; never draw an interaction prompt in a kit or a script: kits that offer an interaction pass their kind to interaction.use.register(entity, label, action, kind) (or interactable.kind on an archetype), and slow uses get a hold (interactable.hold / interaction.system.holdSeconds) instead of a custom timer. Styles and kinds are data (feedback_styles, interaction_kinds): restyle with them, do not recode. Leave the player settings (interaction.feedback.settings) to the menu.
A scheme is a starting proposal: a preset applies its own at creation (create takes controls to pick another one — pass the scheme of the kind of game the user asked for — or none), and any key stays changeable with gripforge_gamekit_configure input.actions { overrides: [{ action, keys, buttons?, disabled? }] } — the action of any kit; those entries always win over the scheme. logic chooses where the kits’ logic runs: wasm = logic of the kits in Rust compiled to wasm (Bevy player), ts = TypeScript KitHost (on request only); default wasm (create takes logic too; action=logic without logic reads it, with logic sets it). A game installing a kit without a Rust module runs on the TypeScript KitHost by itself: logic reports runs: ts and fallback: the kits. delete needs confirm=true. Call this first to create or pick the project, then gripforge_gamekit_installed (existing project) or gripforge_gamekit_install. 0 credits.

action.description: list | create | get | bind | data | controls | logic | delete.

bindings.description: bind: { slot: lib_… | null } — Library item per asset slot declared by the installed kits, null clears. A model bound to a creature slot gets its animations by itself as far as that is free (the answer carries the chain in creatures); see gripforge_gamekit_creatures.

collection.description: data: collection name declared by an installed kit (e.g. missions, npcs, zones).

confirm.description: delete: must be true. The project, its revisions and data are removed.

controls.description: create: the control scheme of the kind of game the user asked for (gameplay choices above: one scheme, usually the only one allowed), applied at creation instead of the preset’s own or of the one the kits suggest; none keeps the kits’ own keys.

documents.description: data: documents to upsert (each with its id), validated against the kit schema.

dry_run.description: controls: true returns the diff of keys without writing.

force.description: controls: also replace a touch layout or a help bar the game edited (kept by default).

kits.description: create: explicit kit toggles { "vehicle.driveable": true, … } on top of the preset. Unchecking a required kit fails with toggle_requires. The default kits (ui.menu, input.remap, settings.graphics, ui.prompts, ui.endscreen, save.persistence, audio.core, i18n.text, ui.theme, input.virtualpad, display.fullscreen, asset.preload, asset.cache, ai.navigation on web) are included unless set to false here — only when the user asked for it.

logic.description: create, logic: wasm = logic of the kits in Rust compiled to wasm (Bevy player), ts = TypeScript KitHost (on request only); default wasm. logic without it reads the current choice.

preset.description: create: preset id whose default kits are installed (gripforge_gamekit_search returns presets).

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Required for get, bind, data, controls, logic and delete.

replace.description: data: true to replace the whole collection with documents.

reset.description: controls: also drop the key overrides the game wrote itself (kept by default), so the game ends exactly on the scheme — what a game made before the schemes needs to move to one. Preview with dry_run.

scheme.description: controls: the control scheme to show (dry_run) or apply — fps, third_person, moba_click, arpg_click, top_down, platformer, fighting, vehicle, rts, point_click: the one of the kind of game (gameplay choices above; a dungeon crawler → arpg_click, a MOBA → moba_click, an RTS → rts). Omit to read the schemes and the project controls.

target.description: create: pass the confirmed engine explicitly (Three.js=web). Ask the user to choose Unity / Godot / Unreal Engine / Three.js before creating if unknown. API default web is for compatibility, not an engine choice.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.

name: gripforge_game_project
title: List, create, read, bind, feed, set the controls of or delete Game Kit projects
